calculator.description1: This calculator is designed to help you determine the impact of your pricing and payment term decisions on Costs, Working Capital and Economic Profit for you and for your suppliers. It will allow you to decide among alternative price and payment term scenarios.
calculator.description2: In order to look at "total cost", we need to consider that changing payment terms is a capital investment decision which impacts not only profitability, but also capital efficiency and Return on Invested Capital (ROIC). Therefore, in order to obtain a complete picture of the economic impact of supplier relationships, we must include the impact of payment terms on total cost and working capital efficiency.
calculator.description3:
For example, if we decrease payment days from 90 days to 60 days, but receive an additional 1% price discount, it has a positive impact on profit.

But we can't look at profitability alone. A payment term decrease of 30 days requires a capital investment to fund the early payment. In effect, it means that the company is investing capital to fund an "early payment project" which will generate a "return" in the form of discounted pricing. If the return is less than the cost of the required invested capital then we do not want to pursue it
calculator.description4: Economic profit provides us with the means to balance profit and working capital efficiency. It measures the cost of the capital we invest in our payment terms. If our Economic Profit (change in profit minus a charge for the capital investment) is positive then we should invest capital in shorter payment terms (or generating capital from longer payment terms). If the cost of capital invested is greater than the profit increase, then the initiative should not be pursued.
